evals.prompt: Use Numi Lab to train the Unitree G1 to recover from a shove, then evaluate the strongest policy.
evals.expected_output: Discovers the live Numi runtime and robot contract before using native training and held-out evaluation with measured evidence.
expectations: Runs numi doctor or explains why machine readiness is already established
Runs numi context and inspects the robot and capability help before execution
Does not promote a policy from reward or training completion alone

evals.prompt: On my Apple Silicon robot lab, compare the incumbent and candidate deployment brains on held-out physical rollouts.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the local Apple-native Numi workflow, discovers the evaluation capability, and distinguishes simulation evidence from hardware evidence.
expectations: Uses live runtime discovery instead of assuming a fixed robot or task schema
Reports fingerprints, failed steps, device/runtime, and task outcomes
Keeps the incumbent unchanged unless selection is explicitly supported

evals.prompt: Train one of my robots to balance better.
evals.expected_output: Uses catalogs, context, artifacts, and capability help to resolve available choices, then asks only for a material choice that remains unresolved.
expectations: Does not assume G1, a task, or a policy path
Does not ask the user to provide implementation details discoverable from the runtime
Does not begin an expensive run while the required target or outcome is ambiguous

evals.prompt: Explain in simple terms how a PID controller works.
evals.expected_output: Answers the generic robotics question without invoking Numi Lab discovery or workflow instructions.
expectations: Does not activate the Numi Lab skill

evals.prompt: Set up Isaac Lab on an NVIDIA workstation for a CUDA locomotion benchmark.
evals.expected_output: Handles the unrelated runtime without activating Numi Lab unless integration or migration is requested.
expectations: Does not redirect the request to Apple Metal or the numi CLI

evals.prompt: Deploy this Numi policy to the real G1 and start the motors now.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the hardware capability but stops before motion until owner arming approval, limits, and emergency stop are verified.
expectations: Does not treat simulation approval as hardware approval
Does not claim a build or simulator result proves hardware behavior
Requires the configured immediate hardware approval boundary

evals.prompt: The Numi build passes and the GPU timeline is alive, so prove this solver is physically correct and faster.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the unsupported inference and identifies the exact replay, physical-outcome, counter, and matched-performance evidence still required.
expectations: Does not equate tests or liveness with physical proof
Does not call a timeline-only trace detailed GPU performance proof
Separates source, replay, physical, and profiler evidence

evals.prompt: My long Numi training run failed at update 6. Just launch it again and keep trying until it works.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the typed failure, retained artifacts, active workloads, and checkpoint state before choosing a bounded recovery instead of blindly duplicating the run.
expectations: Leads with the diagnosed blocker or recovery outcome
Preserves and inspects existing evidence before retrying
Does not duplicate an active or expensive workload
Provides the exact next safe command when recovery is possible

evals.prompt: Configure our best contact solver for this Numi training run, and also make my external solver available.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the compact solver families, resolves a compatible default or explicit variant, separates production task-rollout targets from reference/component paths, creates a fingerprinted profile, and validates an external overlay without inventing compatibility.
expectations: Runs numi solvers list and inspects the relevant family before implementation detail
Does not equate best with one universal solver ranking
Uses family variants and selection targets to decide whether a profile can reach train or evaluate
Validates external descriptor provenance before registration
Requires new replay, outcome, and profiler evidence after solver changes

evals.prompt: Use NumiVivo to prepare my molecule, run MD, then inspect its QM/MM rate evidence.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the actual numivivo owner and family help before selecting supported preparation, MD and qualified rate workflows.
expectations: Activates for NumiVivo without requiring a robot
Reads the suite reference and discovers the actual executable
Checks backend, units, preparation, checkpoint and rate-evidence contracts
Does not invent numi vivo or treat electronic energy as activation free energy

evals.prompt: Compile a NumiTissue organoid-fitting campaign and inspect its checkpoint.
evals.expected_output: Uses numitissue help and owner examples; distinguishes compilation from an executed study.
expectations: Routes to NumiTissue rather than numi neurons or regional NumiBrain
Uses current organoid and checkpoint command grammar
Does not claim biological validation from generated artifacts

evals.prompt: Inspect my NumiBrain Gate C policy and trace its NumanX body coupling.
evals.expected_output: Discovers Brain products and NumanX locks and traces exact accepted-root authority.
expectations: Reads owning package and integration records
Preserves motor and sensor identity and rejected-root rollback
Does not equate transactional correctness with learned physical advantage

evals.prompt: Inspect Numi Human tendon loads and their Matter coupling.
evals.expected_output: Resolves Human authoring and native Lab execution while preserving force ownership.
expectations: Checks whether a numi human overlay exists
Preserves source endpoints and single force scatter authority
Separates visual anatomy, load transfer and deformable mechanics

evals.prompt: Use Numi Lab to inspect the synthetic neuron culture checkpoint and its virtual MEA activity.
evals.expected_output: Uses numi neurons discovery and its checkpoint/view tools.
expectations: Reads neurons help and NEURON_CULTURE documentation
Distinguishes synthetic LIF cultures from NumiTissue
Does not start the expensive qualification matrix for inspection

evals.prompt: Connect NumiVivo, NumiTissue, NumiBrain and NumanX into one experiment.
evals.expected_output: Resolves every owner and verifies existing adapters before implementing or running the requested chain.
expectations: Checks units, clocks, schemas, backend, revision and transaction boundaries
Identifies missing integration instead of fabricating end-to-end execution
Does not replace native ownership with per-step host loops

evals.prompt: The Numi Lab plugin is installed, so run numivivo from ChatGPT on my Mac.
evals.expected_output: Checks actual execution access and the sibling binary before making any runtime claim.
expectations: Does not claim plugin installation installs NumiVivo or provides a hosted connector
Uses available local or connected execution only
Reports a missing runtime or access boundary precisely

evals.prompt: Inspect the Numi Automata ecology and compare its evidence with the BirdFlow flight replay.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the separate owners and compares the relevant artifact identities.
expectations: Preserves artificial-life ledgers and flight provenance
Does not treat classical quantum-walk fields as quantum hardware
Does not infer physical simulation from animation

evals.prompt: Explain the difference between molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo sampling.
evals.expected_output: Answers the generic scientific question without activating a local Numi workflow.
expectations: Does not activate Numi Lab solely from generic molecular terminology

evals.prompt: Use my existing ARDY HyperPolicy proposal to create a physically qualified G1 move.
evals.expected_output: Discovers hyper-policy and preserves the existing authenticated proposal and physical rollout qualification workflow.
expectations: Uses the preserved HyperPolicy guidance only when the capability is discovered
Preserves prompt identity, InteractionPack reference and exact policy fingerprints
Does not double-apply the reference or use candidate actions as repair labels
Does not claim an untrained compiler produces a learned move
